title: terraform module for GPU scaling + health reconciler in private VPC
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Create a reusable Terraform module that provisions GPU node capacity for Redwood Private (VPC) deployments and supports two autoscaling backends: ASG (managed instances) and Karpenter (elastic, spot-friendly). The module must: (1) manage GPU-specific bootstrapping (NVIDIA drivers, device plugin), taints/labels, and mixed-instance policies; (2) expose safe upgrade controls (max_unavailable nodes, surge settings, lifecycle hooks) for rolling OS and runtime upgrades; (3) implement automated health reconciliation: detect non-ready GPU nodes (kernel oops, driver failures, stuck kubelet) and either cordon/drain + terminate or trigger a controlled replacement; (4) support private-subnet-only networking, IAM role attachments, and KMS-encrypted AMI/launch templates. Must be authored as a versioned module with inputs/outputs suitable for both self-managed Private customers and Redwood Dedicated on-prem variants.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module publishes variables documented in the README: gpu_instance_types, desired_capacity, min_size, max_size, autoscaler_backend = ["asg", "karpenter"]
Module creates Launch Template / NodeGroup that boots NVIDIA drivers and installs kubelet + device-plugin via user-data and SSM parameter references
Upgrade path: rolling upgrades respect max_unavailable and drain timeout; documented example in Confluence
Health reconciler runs as a Kubernetes CronJob or external Lambda in the same VPC and successfully replaces unhealthy nodes in a dev cluster without manual intervention
Karpenter mode produces Provisioner CRs with proper taints, GPU resource requests, and nodeSelector for private subnets
All resources include tags (customer_id, environment, module, module_version) and Terraform state references for drift detection
design_decisions: Use a single module with a switch variable autoscaler_backend to emit either ASG resources (launch template + autoscaling group) or Karpenter-style Kubernetes Provisioner CRs
Prefer Launch Templates + mixed instances for ASG to allow GPU extents (g4dn/p4d) in a single group; expose spot_percentage to opt into mixed spot pools
Implement a health reconciler running as a lightweight Kubernetes Deployment by default; offer an option to deploy as Lambda for customers that disallow cluster-level operators
Do not bake GPU drivers into AMIs by default; instead use user-data to install drivers at boot to simplify cross-AMI upgrades and private AMI signing workflows
Expose lifecycle hooks to run graceful drain scripts and a customizable post-terminate hook for node diagnostics upload to a customer s3-compatible endpoint

comments: 2026-03-10 Aisha Banerjee: Scoped ticket during infra sync. Intention is to support both ASG and Karpenter so customers can choose predictable capacity vs elastic spot. Keeping GPU driver install in user-data reduces AMI churn.
2026-03-11 Rafael Gomez: Initial module skeleton pushed to feature branch: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/tree/feat/ENG-11876-gpu-scale-module. Opened draft PR #1456 for early feedback.

2026-03-12 Priya Shah: Reviewed Karpenter CR approach. Suggest exposing separate nodeProvisioner labels for taint/taintEffect and preemptible affinity. Also requested that we add a node readiness exporter to aid health detection.

2026-03-12 SRE: Ran first smoke deploy to private dev cluster (vpc-priv-dev). Observed that GPU device-plugin sometimes fails when kubelet starts before drivers; added a systemd unit retry loop in user-data.

2026-03-13 Aisha Banerjee: Added acceptance test plan and demo app to verify GPU scheduling (ml-inference/benchmark). Need validator for node termination events to avoid N^2 scale-down during reconcilers.

2026-03-13 Rafael Gomez: PR #1456 updated with health reconciler prototype. Marking In Progress — will request formal review once terratest jobs pass. Pending: SSM parameter for private AMI id retrieval and KMS policy review.
notes: Keep drift detection enabled in CI (terraform plan diffs posted to PR) to catch manual nodegroup mutations by customers.
Consider adding a safe-fallback policy: when Karpenter is selected but insufficient capacity is detected, fallback to a small ASG with on-demand GPUs for critical requests.
Performance team requested metric hooks for per-node GPU utilization to enable autoscaler based on GPU memory rather than just CPU. Add as follow-up if time allows.
